items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: The sessions at Jimmy Ryan's ... were presented by Milt Gabler who owned the Commodore Record Shop ... Jack Crystal who worked in Milt's record shop was in charge of the session

ctx.x: and formed the band. But as Rodger could not go into the local, the owner of the club cut his salary off completely. The club was run by a fellow named Oscar who had been the head waiter at Cafe Uptown when it opened in 1940. The orchestra was playing more commercial numbers than jazz because that was what the owner wanted. Business was not good and within two weeks after I had joined the band, the place was closed. We did a radio show/that was the end of Rodger Ray's dream of being a singer and band leader.

I gigged and did many Sunday afternoon jam sessions at Jimmy Ryan's and few in Boston at the Ken Club. Once in Boston I jammed with Pete Brown and another time with Coleman Hawkins. The sessions at Jimmy Ryan's which was across the street from the Famous Door and the three Dances on 52nd Street, were presented by Milt Gabler who owned the Commodore Record Shop near the Grand Central station on East 42nd Street.

Jack Crystal who worked in Milt's record shop was in charge of the session which featured many well known black and white musicians: Art Hodes, Pee Wee Russell, Bobby Hackett, George Wettling, Rod Cless, Sid Catlett, Hank Duncan, Sandy Williams, Wild Bill Davison and Oran "Hot Lips" Page to name a few that participated in these sessions which really jumped.
